stages.sub: How to read a diagram that shows how unequally income or wealth is shared.

steps.q: One person earns a £30,000 salary this year. Another owns a £2 million house bought years ago. Are these two things measuring the same kind of thing?
steps.right: No, one is earned over time, the other is something already owned
steps.wrong: Yes, both just measure how rich someone is right now
steps.hint: One arrives each year in pay packets. The other is a pile of value someone already holds.

steps.q: You want a diagram to show how income is shared across the whole population, from the poorest to the richest. If one axis builds up the share of population and the other builds up the share of income they hold, what would you put along the bottom axis?
steps.right: The running total of the population, poorest first
steps.wrong: The running total of income, richest first
steps.hint: Think about which axis orders people, and which axis adds up their income.

steps.q: Suppose every single person earned exactly the same income. If you plotted the poorest 20% of people against the share of income they hold, what share would they have?
steps.hint: If income is shared perfectly evenly, does any group hold more or less than its population share?

steps.q: In reality the poorest 20% of people usually hold far less than 20% of total income, while the richest hold much more than their share. If you plotted this real pattern point by point, would the line sit on the diagonal or below it?
steps.hint: The poorest hold less than their population share, so the plotted line starts below the equal-share line.

steps.q: Country A's actual line sags a long way below the diagonal. Country B's actual line stays close to the diagonal. Which country has income shared more unevenly?
steps.right: Country A, with the line further from the diagonal
steps.wrong: Country B, with the line closer to the diagonal
steps.hint: The equal-share line is the benchmark. Does being closer to it or further from it mean more evenly shared income?

steps.q: A country's bowed line moves noticeably closer to the diagonal between 2010 and 2020. Since distance from the diagonal shows how uneven the sharing is, what does this shift tell you about that decade?
steps.right: Income inequality fell over the decade
steps.wrong: Income inequality stayed exactly the same
steps.hint: The line moved, so the distance from the equal-share line changed. What does a smaller gap mean?
